patterns.comment: Fully free-form source, which **FREE on the first line opens. The end pattern can never match, so the block runs to the end of the member: a fully free-form member cannot revert to columns part way through.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.allfree

patterns.comment: **FREE itself, which may appear only in column 1 of the first line and must be the only thing on it.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.free.precompiler.allfree

patterns.comment: A whole-line comment: an asterisk in position 7, whatever form type position 6 holds. It runs to the newline.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpgle.fixed

patterns.comment: A // comment, which runs to the end of the line.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpgle.free

patterns.comment: *IN is the indicator array, *INxx a single indicator and *IN(xx) an indexed one. The name may be numbered or one of the named indicators, the same set the fixed-format specifications accept; the rule took only digits, so *INLR and *INOF fell through to the general rule for asterisk words.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.indicator

patterns.comment: A figurative constant or other reserved value, which is written with a leading asterisk: *BLANKS and *ZEROS, *ON and *OFF, *ISO and the rest.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle

patterns.comment: A numeric literal. RPG names may contain $ # @ and, in some code pages, £ and §, none of which are word characters, so a plain word boundary treats the 1 of a field named end#1 as a number. The guards name every character a name may contain instead.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.rpgle

patterns.comment: The reserved words that are not written with a leading asterisk: the user date words UDATE, UDAY, UMONTH and UYEAR, and the page numbering fields PAGE and PAGE1 through PAGE7. The asterisk spellings *DATE, *DAY, *MONTH and *YEAR are covered by the rule for asterisk constants. The surrounding look-arounds keep a name such as MYPAGE or PAGE8 from matching.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle

patterns.comment: The fields of the SQL communications area, which the precompiler brings into the program and SQL sets after every statement.
patterns.name: variable.language.rpgle.sql

rpglecommon.comment: Used in fixed-format and /FREE-within-fixed contexts. Includes gutter-aware fixedcomment and fixedstrings.

freerpglecommon.comment: Used in **FREE (fully free-format) contexts where no sequence-number gutter is present.

patterns.comment: A comment inside an SQL statement. The reference allows SQL's own double hyphen and, in free-form RPG, the ordinary // as well. The scope name also carried the language twice.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpgle.sql

patterns.comment: A bracketed comment, allowed wherever SQL allows a blank and able to span any number of lines. It is not allowed between the keywords EXEC and SQL.
patterns.name: comment.block.rpgle.sql

patterns.comment: The global variables Db2 for i supplies, such as JOB_NAME and CLIENT_IPADDR.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.sql.globals

patterns.comment: The built-in data types, from the built-in-type diagram in the Db2 for i SQL reference. They are matched before the function rule because a type written with a length, as in VARCHAR(30), would otherwise be taken for a function call, and before the reserved word rule because DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP and CHAR are reserved words as well as types. Sorted in reverse so a type is tried before any type it begins with, as with INTEGER before INT.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.sql

patterns.comment: A name immediately followed by an opening parenthesis, which is how a function call is told apart from an ordinary name.
patterns.name: support.function.rpgle.sql

patterns.comment: A name qualified by its schema, written with either a dot or a slash.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.sql.schema

patterns.comment: A host variable, which SQL reads and writes by name and which carries a leading colon.
patterns.name: variable.parameter.rpgle.sql

patterns.comment: Hexadecimal literal in an SQL statement, X'xx'.
patterns.name: string.other.rpgle.sql.hex

patterns.comment: Character literal in an SQL statement. A quote inside a literal is written twice, which closes this match and opens another, the same way the RPG character literal behaves.
patterns.name: string.quoted.single.rpgle.sql

patterns.comment: An asterisk value inside an SQL statement, such as the *NONE and *ENDMOD of SET OPTION. Without this the asterisk was taken for the multiplication operator and the word beside it left unscoped. A letter must follow the asterisk, so the * of SELECT COUNT(*) is untouched.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.sql

patterns.comment: The Db2 for i reserved words, Table 1 of Reserved words in the SQL reference, plus AT, FOUND, SQLERROR and SQLWARNING, which embedded SQL uses in CONNECT and WHENEVER but which are not reserved. Sorted in reverse so a word is tried before any word it begins with, as with YEARS before YEAR. Words that are keywords in a clause but are not reserved, such as PRECEDING, DEFERRED or TEMPORARY, are deliberately left out: a reserved word can never be an identifier, so matching it is safe, while a word that is only a keyword may also be a column name.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.rpgle.sql.reserved

patterns.comment: Numeric literal in an SQL statement. The leading word boundary keeps the rule off the digits of an identifier such as CUST1. A sign in front of a literal is scoped by the operator rule below, as it is elsewhere in the grammar. This sits after the comment and literal rules so digits inside those are not picked out.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.rpgle.sql

patterns.comment: SQL operators: comparison, arithmetic and concatenation. Longer operators are listed first so that >= is one token rather than > followed by =. The comment rule above runs first, so the -- that opens a comment is never seen as two minus signs, and the qualified name rule runs first, so the slash in schema/object is not division. The RPGLE grammar shares this file's reserved word list but has no operator rule yet.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.rpgle.sql

patterns.comment: Program data at the end of the member. Two asterisks open it, and the look-ahead keeps **FREE out because that opens a fully free-form member.
The ** form that names what follows: ** on its own, or **CTDATA with the name of the array the records below it load.
patterns.name: string.other.rpgle.ctarray

patterns.comment: The keywords a free-form declaration may carry. Sorted in reverse so a keyword is tried before any keyword it begins with.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.rpgle.free.definition.keywords

freeidentifiers.comment: Used in **FREE contexts. Delegates to freerpglecommon.

patterns.comment: A name. This is a plain match rather than a block running to the end of the line: as a block its name coloured every unmatched character after the first name, so a semicolon read as a variable, and scoping only the block's opening capture instead left every name after the first one unscoped. The keyword rules are consulted before this one, so a word that is a keyword still reads as one.
patterns.name: variable.other.rpgle.free.definition.identifier

fixedfreeidentifiers.comment: Used in fixed-format and /FREE-within-fixed contexts. Delegates to rpglecommon.

patterns.comment: A name. This is a plain match rather than a block running to the end of the line: as a block its name coloured every unmatched character after the first name, so a semicolon read as a variable, and scoping only the block's opening capture instead left every name after the first one unscoped. The keyword rules are consulted before this one, so a word that is a keyword still reads as one.
patterns.name: variable.other.rpgle.free.definition.identifier

freeformat.comment: Free-format statements for **FREE (fully free-format) source. Uses freerpglecommon throughout.

patterns.comment: The control statement, from CTL-OPT to the semicolon that ends it. The look-ahead opens the block without consuming the word, so that CTL-OPT and its keywords can be scoped separately by the rules inside.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.control

patterns.comment: CTL-OPT itself, the word that opens a control statement.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.free.control

patterns.comment: The keywords a control statement may carry. Sorted in reverse so a keyword is tried before any keyword it begins with.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.rpgle.free.control.keywords

patterns.comment: A file statement, from DCL-F to the semicolon that ends it. As with the control statement the look-ahead leaves the word for the rule inside.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.file

patterns.comment: DCL-F itself, the word that opens a file statement.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.free.file

patterns.comment: The keywords a file statement may carry. Sorted in reverse so a keyword is tried before any keyword it begins with.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.rpgle.free.file.keywords

patterns.comment: BEGSR and ENDSR, which open and close a subroutine. Only the prefix differs, so the two are matched together.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.free.definition.subr

patterns.comment: A declaration that has no matching END word: DCL-S, DCL-C, DCL-PARM and DCL-SUBF. The block ends at the newline, so it covers the line the declaration opens on; a declaration continued onto further lines is picked up by the same rules at the outer level.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.definition.simple

patterns.comment: The DCL- word that opens a declaration with no matching END.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.free.definition.simple

patterns.comment: A // comment ending the declaration line.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpgle.free

patterns.comment: A declaration closed by a matching END word: DCL-DS, DCL-ENUM, DCL-PROC, DCL-PR and DCL-PI. The block ends at the newline, so a one-line form such as DCL-DS ... END-DS is scoped here while the subfields of a multi-line one are scoped at the outer level.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.definition.complex

patterns.comment: The DCL- word that opens a declaration with a matching END.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.free.definition.complex.dcl

patterns.comment: The END word when it is written on the same line as the declaration it closes.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.free.definition.complex.dcl

patterns.comment: A name on the declaration line: the item being declared, and on a one-line data structure its subfields. An RPG name may begin with a letter, an underscore, or one of the currency and national characters.
patterns.name: variable.other.rpgle.free.definition.identifier

patterns.comment: A free-form calculation statement that runs onto another line. The reference states that no directive may be specified within a single free-form calculation statement, and that a line inside one which begins with what looks like a directive is read instead as a slash followed by a name, so that x = y on one line and /title + 5; on the next is a division by a variable called title. This block is what keeps the directive rules away from those lines: it opens only on an assignment whose line carries no semicolon, which is what makes the statement continue, and it holds the ordinary calculation rules with the directives left out. A statement that ends on the line it starts on never opens it.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.calculation.continued

patterns.comment: The END word of a declaration written over more than one line. It is reached at the outer level because the declaration block above ends at the newline.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.free.definition.complex.dcl

patterns.comment: The operation codes that free-form calculations accept, which is Table 124 of the reference. ADDDUR, ALLOC, REALLOC and SHTDN are traditional-syntax only and are written as the built-in functions %ALLOC, %REALLOC and %SHTDN or as duration arithmetic in free form, so they are not here. AND and OR are not here either. Free form dropped the ANDxx and ORxx forms in favour of expressions, so the two words join an expression rather than begin a statement and the connective rule scopes them, alongside NOT. The optional trailing group is the operation extender, the same closed set the fixed-format calculations use. Only the letters are scoped, leaving the parentheses to the surrounding context, which is how the fixed-format extender rule treats them.

fixedfreeformat.comment: Free-format statements for fixed-format source (including mixed-mode files). Uses rpglecommon throughout for gutter awareness.

patterns.comment: The control statement, from CTL-OPT to the semicolon that ends it. The look-ahead opens the block without consuming the word, so that CTL-OPT and its keywords can be scoped separately by the rules inside.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.control

patterns.comment: CTL-OPT itself, the word that opens a control statement.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.free.control

patterns.comment: The keywords a control statement may carry. Sorted in reverse so a keyword is tried before any keyword it begins with.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.rpgle.free.control.keywords

patterns.comment: A file statement, from DCL-F to the semicolon that ends it. As with the control statement the look-ahead leaves the word for the rule inside.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.file

patterns.comment: DCL-F itself, the word that opens a file statement.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.free.file

patterns.comment: The keywords a file statement may carry. Sorted in reverse so a keyword is tried before any keyword it begins with.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.rpgle.free.file.keywords

patterns.comment: BEGSR and ENDSR, which open and close a subroutine. Only the prefix differs, so the two are matched together.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.free.definition.subr

patterns.comment: A declaration that has no matching END word: DCL-S, DCL-C, DCL-PARM and DCL-SUBF. The block ends at the newline, so it covers the line the declaration opens on; a declaration continued onto further lines is picked up by the same rules at the outer level.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.definition.simple

patterns.comment: The DCL- word that opens a declaration with no matching END.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.free.definition.simple

patterns.comment: A // comment ending the declaration line.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpgle.free

patterns.comment: A declaration closed by a matching END word: DCL-DS, DCL-ENUM, DCL-PROC, DCL-PR and DCL-PI. The block ends at the newline, so a one-line form such as DCL-DS ... END-DS is scoped here while the subfields of a multi-line one are scoped at the outer level.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.definition.complex

patterns.comment: The DCL- word that opens a declaration with a matching END.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.free.definition.complex.dcl

patterns.comment: The END word when it is written on the same line as the declaration it closes.
patterns.name: storage.type.rpgle.free.definition.complex.dcl

patterns.comment: A name on the declaration line: the item being declared, and on a one-line data structure its subfields. An RPG name may begin with a letter, an underscore, or one of the currency and national characters.
patterns.name: variable.other.rpgle.free.definition.identifier

patterns.comment: A free-form calculation statement that runs onto another line. The reference states that no directive may be specified within a single free-form calculation statement, and that a line inside one which begins with what looks like a directive is read instead as a slash followed by a name, so that x = y on one line and /title + 5; on the next is a division by a variable called title. This block is what keeps the directive rules away from those lines: it opens only on an assignment whose line carries no semicolon, which is what makes the statement continue, and it holds the ordinary calculation rules with the directives left out. A statement that ends on the line it starts on never opens it. It is anchored after the gutter rather than at the line start, because the gutter rule matches from column 1 and would otherwise take the line start away from it. Positions 6 and 7 must be blank, as they must be for any free-form statement in a column-limited member.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.calculation.continued

tempfreeformat.comment: Handles /FREE.../END-FREE blocks within fixed-format source. Uses fixedfreeformat and fixedfreeSQL for gutter awareness.

patterns.comment: A /FREE block in a column-limited member. The reference records the directive as no longer needed, but the compiler still checks it and real source still carries it.
The /FREE directive that opens the block, taking the gutter and form type ahead of it with it.
patterns.name: keyword.control.rpgle.precompiler

patterns.comment: The directive that closes a /FREE block. Matched at the directive itself rather than from the start of the line: anchored to the line start it won on leftmost position over the rule that scopes a directive and its form type separately, so /END-FREE came out as one span where /FREE came out as two.
patterns.name: keyword.control.rpgle.precompiler

patterns.comment: A whole-line comment: an asterisk in position 7, whatever form type position 6 holds.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpgle.fixed

patterns.comment: Positions 1-5, the page and line number, which the compiler ignores.
patterns.name: comment.gutter

patterns.comment: The form type in position 6. It travels with the gutter and the comment rules because a literal continued onto another line carries one on every line it spans. The look-ahead leaves C+ and C/ alone: those are the continuation and directive markers of embedded SQL and a precompiler directive, which have rules of their own.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.fixed.specs

patterns.comment: Positions 81-100, the comment area of a fixed-format specification. The look-ahead requires something to actually be there, because a line of exactly 80 characters would otherwise open the block at the line break with nothing to close it, swallowing the line below. The end is a zero-width look-ahead so the block does not consume the line ending out from under an enclosing literal.
patterns.name: comment.block.line.rpgle.fixed

patterns.comment: The form type in position 6, which is what makes a line fixed-format and decides which specification's rules apply to the rest of it.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.fixed.specs

patterns.comment: Everything after the form type on a control specification. The block opens just past position 6 and closes at the newline, so each entry rule inside it counts its columns from the form type.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.h

patterns.comment: Control specification keywords, positions 7-80. A keyword may begin in column 7, immediately after the H in column 6, where there is no word boundary, so the leading anchor accepts either that position or an ordinary boundary. Sorted in reverse so a longer keyword is tried before a shorter one it begins with.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.rpgle.fixed.h.keywords

patterns.comment: Everything after the form type on a file specification. The block opens just past position 6 and closes at the newline, so each entry rule inside it counts its columns from the form type.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.f

patterns.comment: File specification position 17, the file type: I for input, O for output, U for update and C for combined.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.f.type

patterns.comment: File specification position 18, the file designation: P for primary, S for secondary, R for record address, T for table or array, F for full procedural.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.f.designation

patterns.comment: File specification position 19, E when the file is to signal end of file.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.f.eof

patterns.comment: File specification position 20, A when records may be added to the file.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.f.addition

patterns.comment: File specification position 21, the sequence in which a match-field file is read: A for ascending, D for descending.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.f.sequence

patterns.comment: File specification position 22, the file format: E when the file is externally described, F when the program describes it.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.f.format

patterns.comment: File specification positions 23-27, the record length. Only a program described file has one, so the F in position 22 is required first.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.fi.recordlen

patterns.comment: File specification position 28, L when the file is read by limits.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.f.limitproc

patterns.comment: File specification positions 29-33, the length of the key field. Only a program described file gives one, hence the F in position 22.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.fi.keyfieldlen

patterns.comment: File specification position 34, the record address type, which says how the key is held: K for keyed, A, P, G, D, T, Z and F for the rest.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.f.addrtype

patterns.comment: File specification position 35, the organisation of a program described file: I for indexed, T for record address.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.fi.fileorg

patterns.comment: File specification positions 36-42, the device the file is attached to.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.f.device

patterns.comment: The keywords a file specification may carry in positions 44-80. Sorted in reverse so a keyword is tried before any keyword it begins with.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.rpgle.fixed.f

patterns.comment: Everything after the form type on a definition specification. The block opens just past position 6 and closes at the newline, so each entry rule inside it counts its columns from the form type.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.d

patterns.comment: The argument of EXTFMT, which is a closed set: B binary, C UCS-2, I integer, L leading sign, R trailing sign, P packed, S zoned, U unsigned, F float. Every other keyword whose values are a closed set spells them with a leading asterisk or as digits, so the figurative constant and numeric rules already reach those; EXTFMT is the only one written as a bare letter.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.d.extfmt

patterns.comment: A literal closes on its quote, or at the end of the line, but not where the line ends in a hyphen or a plus, which the reference defines as continuing it on the next line. The third alternative handles a line that carries a comment in 81-100: the literal ends at the last non-blank of the specification area rather than of the line, so a continuation character followed by padding out to column 80 still continues even with a comment to its right.
patterns.name: string.quoted.single.rpgle.fixed

patterns.comment: The continuation character that carries a literal onto the next line, where it is the last non-blank of the line.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.continuation

patterns.comment: The same, on a fixed-format line that pads out to column 80 and carries a comment in 81-100. Only the character is scoped.
The form type in position 6, matched again inside a specification block so that a continued line carrying its own form type is scoped.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.fixed.specs

patterns.comment: A name too long for positions 7-21, or one the programmer chose to split, written on a continued name line that ends in an ellipsis.
patterns.name: variable.other.rpgle.fixed.d.extended.name

patterns.comment: Definition specification position 22, E when the item is externally described.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.d.external

patterns.comment: Definition specification position 23, the kind of data structure: S for the program status structure, U for a data area.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.d.dstype

patterns.comment: Definition specification positions 24-25, what is being defined: DS, PI, PR, S for a standalone field or C for a named constant.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.d.dectype

patterns.comment: Definition specification positions 26-32, from position. The reference allows 1 to 9999999 right adjusted, so the entry is seven wide. The lookahead keeps the rule off an entry that is entirely blank, which is the common case for a subfield defined by length alone.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.d.from

patterns.comment: Definition specification positions 33-39, to position or length. The reference allows 1 to 9999999 right adjusted, so the entry is seven wide and a full seven digit value must match. A signed value is the older fixed-format spelling of a LIKE length adjustment; current releases write that as the second parameter of the LIKE keyword instead. The lookahead keeps the rule off an entry that is entirely blank.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.d.to

patterns.comment: Definition specification position 40, internal data type. A character, B binary, C UCS-2, D date, F float, G graphic, I integer, N indicator, O object, P packed, S zoned, T time, U unsigned, Z timestamp, * pointer.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.d.datatype

patterns.comment: Definition specification positions 41-42, the number of decimal positions.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.d.decpos

patterns.comment: Definition specification keywords, positions 44-80. Sorted in reverse so a longer keyword is tried before a shorter one it begins with, as with LIKEDS before LIKE.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.rpgle.fixed.d.keywords

patterns.comment: Everything after the form type on a input specification. The block opens just past position 6 and closes at the newline, so each entry rule inside it counts its columns from the form type.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.i

patterns.comment: Input specification positions 31-34, data attributes: the external date or time format of a date, time or timestamp field, or *VAR for a variable-length character, graphic or UCS-2 field. Anchored on columns 7-20 being blank, which is what distinguishes a field description line from a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.attrs

patterns.comment: Input specification position 35, the separator character of a date or time field. Anchored on columns 7-20 being blank, which is what distinguishes a field description line from a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.sep

patterns.comment: Input specification position 36, data format. A character, C UCS-2, G graphic, B binary, F float, I integer, L or R zoned with a leading or trailing sign, N indicator, P packed, S zoned, U unsigned, D date, T time, Z timestamp. Anchored on columns 7-20 being blank, which is what distinguishes a field description line from a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.fmt

patterns.comment: Input specification positions 37-41, the starting position of the field in the record, right adjusted. Anchored on columns 7-20 being blank, which is what distinguishes a field description line from a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.from

patterns.comment: Input specification positions 42-46, the end position of the field in the record, right adjusted. Anchored on columns 7-20 being blank, which is what distinguishes a field description line from a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.to

patterns.comment: Input specification positions 47-48, decimal positions of a numeric field. Anchored on columns 7-20 being blank, which is what distinguishes a field description line from a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.decpos

patterns.comment: Input specification positions 63-64, control level: L1 through L9. Anchored on columns 7-20 being blank, which is what distinguishes a field description line from a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.ctrl

patterns.comment: Input specification positions 65-66, matching fields: M1 through M9. Anchored on columns 7-20 being blank, which is what distinguishes a field description line from a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.matching

patterns.comment: Input specification positions 67-68, field record relation. Anchored on columns 7-20 being blank, which is what distinguishes a field description line from a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.fldrcdrel

patterns.comment: Input specification positions 69-70, the field indicator set on when a numeric field is greater than zero. Anchored on columns 7-20 being blank, which is what distinguishes a field description line from a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.posfld

patterns.comment: Input specification positions 71-72, the field indicator set on when a numeric field is less than zero. Anchored on columns 7-20 being blank, which is what distinguishes a field description line from a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.negfld

patterns.comment: Input specification positions 73-74, the field indicator set on when the field is zero or blank. Anchored on columns 7-20 being blank, which is what distinguishes a field description line from a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.zerofld

patterns.comment: Input specification positions 17-18, the sequence, which orders the record types of a program described file.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.seq

patterns.comment: Input specification position 19, number. 1 means only one record of this type may appear in the sequenced group, N means one or more.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.number

patterns.comment: Input specification position 20, O when the record type is optional.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.option

patterns.comment: Input specification positions 21-22, record identifying indicator: 01-99, L1-L9 or LR, H1-H9, U1-U8, RT, or ** for a look-ahead line. Guarded on columns 7-20 not being all blank, the same way the identification codes are, so an external field name in 21-30 of a field description line cannot be read as an indicator.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.recordid

patterns.comment: Input specification record identification code. Columns 23-46 carry three codes of eight characters on an identification line, but the same columns carry the data attributes, format and field location of a field description line. The two are told apart by columns 7-20, which hold the file name or AND/OR on an identification line and are always blank on a field description line. The alternation asserts that those columns are not all blank; it is written out because Oniguruma requires a lookbehind to be of fixed length and rejects a lookahead inside one.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.i.pos1

patterns.comment: Everything after the form type on a calculation specification. The block opens just past position 6 and closes at the newline, so each entry rule inside it counts its columns from the form type.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.c

patterns.comment: Calculation specification positions 7-8, control level. L0 is total calculation time, L1-L9 a control break, LR after the last record, SR a subroutine, and AN or OR continue the conditioning indicators from the line above.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.c.ctrl

patterns.comment: Calculation specification positions 9-11, the conditioning indicator, optionally negated by N in the first of them.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.c.n01

patterns.comment: An operation taking an expression, which occupies positions 36-80 rather than the separate factor 2, result and length entries. The longer names are listed before the shorter ones they begin with, so FOR-EACH is not read as FOR, and an optional extender in parentheses is taken with the operation. A letter or hyphen may not follow the name, so FOR does not open the block on a FORCE operation, which is an ordinary calculation.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.fixed.c.extfactor2

patterns.comment: Calculation specification positions 26-35, an operation code carrying a comparison suffix. The suffix is GT, LT, EQ, NE, GE or LE, or two blanks for the unsuffixed form of CAB and CAS.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.fixed.c.operation

patterns.comment: A name, a parenthesis or the per cent that opens a built-in function, anywhere in the calculation entries. RPG names may start with the currency and national characters as well as a letter.
patterns.name: variable.other

patterns.comment: Calculation specification positions 26-35, an operation code carrying a comparison suffix. The suffix is GT, LT, EQ, NE, GE or LE, or two blanks for the unsuffixed form of CAB and CAS.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.fixed.c.operation

patterns.comment: Calculation specification positions 26-35, the operation code. Sorted in reverse so a longer code is tried before a shorter one it begins with, as with ADDDUR before ADD and FOR-EACH before FOR. A letter or hyphen may not follow the code, so END is not matched inside a misspelling such as end-monitor.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.fixed.c.operation

patterns.comment: Calculation specification positions 64-68, the length of the result field when the calculation defines it.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.c.len

patterns.comment: Calculation specification positions 69-70, the decimal positions of the result field.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.c.decpos

patterns.comment: Calculation specification the high resulting indicator. 01-99, KA-KN and KP-KY function keys, H1-H9, L1-L9, LR, MR, OA-OG and OV overflow, U1-U8, or RT.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.c.hi

patterns.comment: Calculation specification the low resulting indicator. 01-99, KA-KN and KP-KY function keys, H1-H9, L1-L9, LR, MR, OA-OG and OV overflow, U1-U8, or RT.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.c.lo

patterns.comment: Calculation specification the equal resulting indicator. 01-99, KA-KN and KP-KY function keys, H1-H9, L1-L9, LR, MR, OA-OG and OV overflow, U1-U8, or RT.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.c.eq

patterns.comment: An operation extender, in positions 26-35 to the right of the operation code and inside parentheses. The eleven extenders are a closed set: A always or ascending, H half adjust, N no lock, P pad, D operational descriptors or date or descending, T time, Z timestamp, M default precision, R result decimal precision, E error handling and C current procedure. Only the letters are scoped; the reference allows blanks for readability, so MULT(H), MULT (H) and MULT ( H ) are all valid.
Everything after the form type on a output specification. The block opens just past position 6 and closes at the newline, so each entry rule inside it counts its columns from the form type.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.o

patterns.comment: Output specification position 17, the record type: H for heading, D for detail, T for total and E for exception.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.type

patterns.comment: Positions 18-20, record addition and deletion. ADD is valid for input, output and update files; DEL only for update DISK files. These occupy the same position 18 that holds fetch overflow or release, so a line carries one or the other.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.addel

patterns.comment: Output specification position 18, F to fetch the overflow routine or R to release the record.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.fetch

patterns.comment: Output specification positions 21-23, the first output indicator.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.n01

patterns.comment: Output specification positions 24-26, the second output indicator.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.n02

patterns.comment: Output specification positions 27-29, the third output indicator.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.n03

patterns.comment: Positions 40-42, space before. Only a record identification line has these; on a field description line the same columns hold the edit code, blank after and end position, so the look-behind requires a non-blank somewhere in 7-20. At least one digit is required so a run of blanks is not scoped.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.spacebefore

patterns.comment: Positions 43-45, space after. Only a record identification line has these; on a field description line the same columns hold the edit code, blank after and end position, so the look-behind requires a non-blank somewhere in 7-20. At least one digit is required so a run of blanks is not scoped.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.spaceafter

patterns.comment: Positions 46-48, skip before. Only a record identification line has these; on a field description line the same columns hold the edit code, blank after and end position, so the look-behind requires a non-blank somewhere in 7-20. At least one digit is required so a run of blanks is not scoped.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.skipbefore

patterns.comment: Positions 49-51, skip after. Only a record identification line has these; on a field description line the same columns hold the edit code, blank after and end position, so the look-behind requires a non-blank somewhere in 7-20. At least one digit is required so a run of blanks is not scoped.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.skipafter

patterns.comment: Position 52, data format. Blank writes a numeric field as zoned decimal and a character field as stored. A field description line is the one that leaves positions 7-20 blank, which is what separates these from the space and skip entries occupying the same columns on a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.dataformat

patterns.comment: Positions 47-51, the end position of the field in the output record. At least one digit is required so a run of blanks is not scoped. A field description line is the one that leaves positions 7-20 blank, which is what separates these from the space and skip entries occupying the same columns on a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.endpos

patterns.comment: Position 45, blank after. B resets the field once it has been written. A field description line is the one that leaves positions 7-20 blank, which is what separates these from the space and skip entries occupying the same columns on a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.blankafter

patterns.comment: Position 44, edit code. 1-4 combine commas and zero balances, A-D add a CR sign, J-M a trailing minus and N-Q a leading minus; 5-9 are the user-defined codes; X forces a hexadecimal F sign, Y edits a date and Z suppresses leading zeros. A field description line is the one that leaves positions 7-20 blank, which is what separates these from the space and skip entries occupying the same columns on a record identification line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.o.editcode

patterns.comment: Everything after the form type on a procedure specification. The block opens just past position 6 and closes at the newline, so each entry rule inside it counts its columns from the form type.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.p

patterns.comment: A continued name line. Any procedure name may be split by ending the partial name with an ellipsis, and one longer than the fifteen positions of the name entry has to be. The whole partial name is taken together with its ellipsis so the three dots are not read as punctuation, which matches how the definition specification handles the same construct.
patterns.name: variable.other.rpgle.fixed.p.extended.name

patterns.comment: Procedure specification position 24, B on the line that begins a subprocedure and E on the line that ends it.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpgle.fixed.p.beginend

patterns.comment: The four procedure keywords, in positions 44-80, and only a begin line may carry them. The look-behind matches the first keyword, which starts in 44; the word boundary matches the ones after it, because more than one keyword may appear on the same line. This is the same shape the control specification uses, and like the definition and file specifications it will also match a name that happens to be spelled like a keyword.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.rpgle.fixed.p.keywords

patterns.comment: An SQL statement in the traditional form. The look-ahead opens the block without consuming C/EXEC SQL, leaving it to the rule inside.
C/EXEC SQL, which opens a traditional embedded SQL statement.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.sql

patterns.comment: The C+ that continues a traditional SQL statement and the C/ that ends it.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.fixed.specs

patterns.comment: The marker that closes a fixed-format SQL statement. The form type is taken with it, the way C/EXEC SQL takes its own, so the two ends of the statement read alike.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.sql

patterns.comment: /TITLE, which names the heading printed at the top of each page of the compiler listing. The directive begins in column 7 or later, so the capture ahead of the slash takes the form type in position 6 and any blanks after it.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.precompiler.title

patterns.comment: The heading text, which is the rest of the line. The reference has it printed on the listing rather than read as code.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpgle.fixed.precompiler.title

patterns.comment: /COPY or /INCLUDE, which name a member whose records are inserted here. The two spellings mean the same thing to the compiler and differ only in how the SQL precompiler treats them. The whole line is taken in one pattern so the member name comes out as a single span. The directive begins in column 7 or later, so the capture ahead of the slash takes the form type in position 6 and any blanks after it.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.precompiler.include

4.comment: The member being brought in, which may be qualified by the file and library it lives in, or given as a path.
4.name: string.other.rpgle.precompiler.include

5.comment: Anything after the member name, which the reference records as an optional comment.
5.name: comment.other.rpgle.precompiler.include

patterns.comment: A conditional compilation block. Both /IF and /ENDIF are consumed by the block rather than left to be matched elsewhere, so the directive that closes it is scoped like the one that opened it and a nested block pairs with its own /ENDIF. /ELSEIF and /ELSE are matched from inside because they do not open a block of their own. The directive begins in column 7 or later, so the capture ahead of the slash takes the form type in position 6 and any blanks after it. A block brackets whatever the member itself may hold, so it reaches the same rules the root patterns do and in the same order. Compile-time data is the one thing left out: the reference allows any source line except that one between the directives of a block.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.precompiler.conditional

patterns.comment: /ELSEIF and /ELSE, which continue the block the enclosing /IF opened. ELSEIF comes first so the longer word wins.
The condition being tested, which asks whether a name has been defined.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.fixed.precompiler.defcheck

patterns.comment: /CHARCOUNT, which sets how the compiler counts the characters of a literal. Those two values are the whole set. The directive begins in column 7 or later, so the capture ahead of the slash takes the form type in position 6 and any blanks after it.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.precompiler.charcount

patterns.comment: /OVERLOAD, which asks the compiler to report how it chose between the candidate prototypes of an overloaded call. Those two values are the whole set. The directive begins in column 7 or later, so the capture ahead of the slash takes the form type in position 6 and any blanks after it.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.precompiler.overload

patterns.comment: /EJECT, which starts a new page of the compiler listing. It takes no operand: the reference requires at least two blanks after it and records the remaining columns as a comment, so the rest of the line is scoped as one. The directive begins in column 7 or later, so the capture ahead of the slash takes the form type in position 6 and any blanks after it.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.precompiler.eject

patterns.comment: /SPACE, which spaces the compiler listing by a count of 1 through 112. The count is followed by at least two blanks and the reference records the remaining columns as a comment, so the rest of the line is scoped as one. The count is optional in the pattern only so that a line missing it still highlights as a directive. The directive begins in column 7 or later, so the capture ahead of the slash takes the form type in position 6 and any blanks after it.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.precompiler.space

patterns.comment: /DEFINE and /UNDEFINE, which add a condition name to the list of currently defined conditions or take it off again. The name is the one /IF DEFINED tests, so it is scoped the same way there and here. The reference requires the rest of the line to be blank, and the predefined conditions the compiler supplies cannot be used with either directive. The directive begins in column 7 or later, so the capture ahead of the slash takes the form type in position 6 and any blanks after it.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.precompiler.define

patterns.comment: The directives that take no special handling. The ones with an operand of their own are listed above and match first; what is left either takes a name, a control keyword, or nothing at all. The directive begins in column 7 or later, so the capture ahead of the slash takes the form type in position 6 and any blanks after it.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.precompiler.misc

patterns.comment: The rest of the directive line, which is the operand it takes.
patterns.name: keyword.control.rpgle.precompiler

patterns.comment: A conditional directive written inside a single free-form statement, which the reference allows for /IF, /ELSEIF, /ELSE and /ENDIF and for no other directive. It matches one line instead of opening a block, because a block would run past the semicolon that ends the statement and take the statement apart. The block form cannot match here: it is anchored at column 1 so that it can carry the gutter, and inside a statement the gutter rule has already taken those columns.
patterns.name: rpgle.fixed.precompiler.conditional

patterns.comment: The condition being tested, which asks whether a name has been defined.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.fixed.precompiler.defcheck

patterns.comment: /TITLE, which names the heading printed at the top of each page of the compiler listing. In fully free-form source a directive may begin in column 1 or later.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.precompiler.title

patterns.comment: The heading text, which is the rest of the line. The reference has it printed on the listing rather than read as code.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpgle.free.precompiler.title

patterns.comment: /COPY or /INCLUDE, which name a member whose records are inserted here. The two spellings mean the same thing to the compiler and differ only in how the SQL precompiler treats them. The whole line is taken in one pattern so the member name comes out as a single span. In fully free-form source a directive may begin in column 1 or later.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.precompiler.include

4.comment: The member being brought in, which may be qualified by the file and library it lives in, or given as a path.
4.name: string.other.rpgle.precompiler.include

5.comment: Anything after the member name, which the reference records as an optional comment.
5.name: comment.other.rpgle.precompiler.include

patterns.comment: /OVERLOAD, which asks the compiler to report how it chose between the candidate prototypes of an overloaded call. Those two values are the whole set.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.precompiler.overload

patterns.name: rpgle.free.precompiler.eject

patterns.comment: The directives that take no special handling. The ones with an operand of their own are listed above and match first; what is left either takes a name, a control keyword, or nothing at all.
patterns.name: rpgle.free.precompiler.misc

patterns.comment: The rest of the directive line, which is the operand it takes.
patterns.name: keyword.control.rpgle.precompiler

patterns.comment: A conditional directive written inside a single free-form statement, which the reference allows for /IF, /ELSEIF, /ELSE and /ENDIF and for no other directive. patterns.comment: The condition being tested, which asks whether a name has been defined.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.free.precompiler.defcheck

patterns.comment: The arithmetic, comparison and assignment operators, including the compound forms such as += and **=.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.rpgle

patterns.comment: Separators and the words that join an expression. IN steps aside when a parenthesis follows it, because that is the data area operation with its extender rather than the connective of a FOR-EACH.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle

patterns.comment: The built-in functions, which all begin with a per cent sign. Sorted in reverse so a function is tried before any function it begins with.
patterns.name: support.function.rpgle.bif

strings.comment: String literals for **FREE (fully free-format) source. A // comment line nested first so any ' inside a comment cannot prematurely close the string.

patterns.comment: A literal closes on its quote, or at the end of the line, but not where the line ends in a hyphen or a plus, which the reference defines as continuing it on the next line. The third alternative handles a line that carries a comment in 81-100: the literal ends at the last non-blank of the specification area rather than of the line, so a continuation character followed by padding out to column 80 still continues even with a comment to its right.
patterns.name: string.other.rpgle.hex

patterns.comment: The continuation character that carries a literal onto the next line, where it is the last non-blank of the line.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.continuation

patterns.comment: The same, on a fixed-format line that pads out to column 80 and carries a comment in 81-100. Only the character is scoped.
A // comment on a line of its own inside a continued literal. The compiler skips it without ending the literal.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpgle.free

patterns.comment: A literal closes on its quote, or at the end of the line, but not where the line ends in a hyphen or a plus, which the reference defines as continuing it on the next line. The third alternative handles a line that carries a comment in 81-100: the literal ends at the last non-blank of the specification area rather than of the line, so a continuation character followed by padding out to column 80 still continues even with a comment to its right.
patterns.name: string.quoted.single.rpgle

patterns.comment: The continuation character that carries a literal onto the next line, where it is the last non-blank of the line.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpgle.continuation

patterns.comment: The same, on a fixed-format line that pads out to column 80 and carries a comment in 81-100. Only the character is scoped.
A // comment on a line of its own inside a continued literal. The compiler skips it without ending the literal.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpgle.free

fixedstrings.comment: String literals for fixed-format source. A // free-format comment handler is nested first to consume any comment line (including any ' it contains) before the gutter-only fixedcomment rule runs.

patterns.comment: A literal closes on its quote, or at the end of the line, but not where the line ends in a hyphen or a plus, which the reference defines as continuing it on the next line. The third alternative handles a line that carries a comment in 81-100: the literal ends at the last non-blank of the specification area rather than of the line, so a continuation character followed by padding out to column 80 still continues even with a comment to its right.

patterns.comment: A literal closes on its quote, or at the end of the line, but not where the line ends in a hyphen or a plus, which the reference defines as continuing it on the next line. The third alternative handles a line that carries a comment in 81-100: the literal ends at the last non-blank of the specification area rather than of the line, so a continuation character followed by padding out to column 80 still continues even with a comment to its right.
